chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Condon, Mezzrow and Armstrong's hangers-on in the studio
summary: Eddie Condon, Mezz Mezzrow and others followed Armstrong to every record date, so the studio held more bystanders than band members.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, in the discography, it's mentioned that Eddie Condon was on banjo and Lonnie Johnson was on guitar on this "I Can't Give You Anything But Love" session. Do you remember Eddie Condon being there?

Yeah, he was... Well, he was in the studio every time Pops was. He was in the studio. You know what I mean? Yeah, he was the studio every time Pops made a record. Not only him, all his boys. Oh, there was a bunch of them. Mezz Mezzrow, you know, the Reefer King? Yeah, he was there. All them boys. They used to follow him around
like he was a (?)sea dog(?) or something.
Well, now, the studios didn't have a limit on how many people could come?

Not as far as he was concerned. Not as far as Louis. Louis was the King. They were trying to make them some money. Oh, he was a big asset to any company was goin' for. Oh, he had all his boys down there, all or any of them. The studio be full of more bystanders around there than there was in the band. Sure. That's why half the time I can't remember who was in the band or who was just lookin' on.
Yeah, he had his boys. Well, they was behind him, because they was... They was followin' him around like a (?)sea dog(?).
